survivors.claim: The done-duplicate refusal on `add` (the iteration-1 s3 fix) names `spec-queue move <ref> <n>` as its remedy, but `move` on a done item exits 2 `already done`, so for this one branch the named remedy cannot succeed. D5 dictates the message form (`already queued at position <n> — spec-queue move <ref> <n>`) with no done-item variant, so this is advisory: the honest remedy for a done duplicate is 'nothing — it is already done', which the spec's locked wording has no slot for.
survivors.impact: A user who re-adds a brief that already shipped is told to run a reorder command that will itself refuse, instead of being told the brief is simply finished.
survivors.evidence: Fixture: brief 05 with one `status: done` spec; items=[{q1, brief 05}]. `spec-queue add 05` → exit 2, stderr `spec-queue: brief 05 is already queued at position 1 (done) — spec-queue move 05 <n> to reorder it`, file byte-identical (correct per D5). Same fixture: `spec-queue move 05 1` → exit 2, stderr `spec-queue: "05" is already done — nothing to move`. Hunk: `const posDesc = pendPos !== -1 ? ... : \`position ${dupIdx + 1} (done)\`` followed by the unconditional `— spec-queue move ${ref} <n> to reorder it`.
